He also says he is not sure quitting was right and might return to a lab. Separately, Peter Wildeford quotes David Sacks calling recursive self-improvement "the most dangerous thing anybody can be working on," and Buck Shlegeris puts the chance of superintelligence within a year at about one in three.

Why it matters: Claims of near-term self-improving AI are moving from fringe talk to insiders and policymakers, which raises pressure for oversight.

It then rented 89 GPUs through RunPod to render 3,220 frames for a little over $20, and Brown says knowing it had cloud compute made Claude Code "much more ambitious."

Why it matters: Agents that can rent compute on their own can take on much larger creative jobs for little money.

title: Cursor's security postmortem traces a breach through stored agent traces
description:
Cursor has published an update on its recent security incident, which @m4rio_eth summarizes as a chain: an exposed Fireworks AI key gave access to stored AI agent traces, unredacted secrets pulled from those traces allowed a pivot into Cursor's internal SaaS systems, and stolen credentials were used to compromise extension delivery, with a malicious Claude Code extension distributed to up to 5,000 users. Malte Ubl says the TL;dr is that static credentials leaked through stolen LLM transcripts, and argues in a Vercel blog post that the only real fix is to end long-lived static credentials.

Why it matters: Agent transcripts often contain secrets, so storing them opens a new path for attackers into developer tools.

Why it matters: Side-by-side runs give teams a rough sense of what open models can handle on long agent jobs.

title: Toby Ord estimates how quickly AI gains slow with more RL, inference and pretraining compute
description:
In a long thread crediting Allan Dafoe, Toby Ord argues that a model's odds of succeeding on benchmark tasks grow as a power law in compute. His preliminary estimates: going from 20% to 80% often took about 10,000x more RL compute (an exponent of about 0.3) but only about 100x more inference compute (about 0.6), with pretraining perhaps near 0.9, so returns are sublinear but "much better than logarithmic."

Why it matters: The exponents hint at where extra compute buys the most capability, which shapes how labs split their spending.

title: One night of sound pulses timed to deep sleep improved memory in early Alzheimer’s, a preprint reports
description:

It is a not-yet-peer-reviewed preprint testing a single night, but a non-invasive sleep device could become a low-risk memory aid if larger trials hold up. Not medical advice.

Grok Bot says it can now join meetings, where people can ask it questions, assign it work or have it keep track of what the team decides. It is available on Super, Ultra, all Team and Enterprise plans as part of a 1.0 release, and the launch post drew more than 2,500 likes and 420,000 views. Michael Truell called it an early beta and predicted that within a couple of quarters it will be normal for work meetings to include bots, a post that drew about 1,400 likes.

Why it matters: Agents are moving from chat windows into live meetings, where they can pick up tasks the moment a team assigns them.

title: Google rolls out Dynamic Workflows in Antigravity

Varun Mohan says the feature is heavily used internally to orchestrate Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Carbon. Sundar Pichai's weekly recap lists two new 8th-gen TPUs, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Robotics 2.5, AlphaGenome 2, the Gemini Decisions API and Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

Why it matters: Scripted workflows give developers repeatable control over multi-agent jobs instead of hoping a long prompt behaves the same way twice.

title: Claude, the API and Claude Code hit a major outage

Why it matters: Teams that run work through one AI provider are exposed when it goes down, as they were with this week's Microsoft 365 outage.

title: llama.cpp ships version 1.0
description:

Why it matters: A stable 1.0 makes the most widely used local-inference engine safer for companies to build products on.

title: TSMC and ASE expand advanced chip packaging in Taiwan
description:
TSMC signed a 7-year deal, running through 2033, with its affiliate Xintec to build and run a line for the "on-substrate" part of CoWoS packaging in central Taiwan, with output targeted for 2029, per a Xintec filing cited by Taiwan media. ASE also opened a new advanced packaging plant in Kaohsiung and broke ground on another, a total NT$100 billion investment.

Why it matters: CoWoS packaging is a key bottleneck for AI chips, so new capacity affects how many GPUs can ship.

title: DeepSeek opens the full DeepSeek App feature set through its API
description:
DeepSeek says the capabilities behind its app (search, files, links, safety and voice) are now available through the DeepSeek API, switched on with a few parameters, plus standalone OCR, speech-recognition and text-to-speech APIs. V4.1-Flash now supports these tools across the Messages, Responses and Chat Completions formats with tool calls handled server-side, tool use is billed on top of token charges, and an open-source frontend demo can import DeepSeek chat history. The launch thread drew more than 450 likes in its first minutes.

Why it matters: Developers can build a full DeepSeek-style assistant without wiring up search, files and voice themselves.

title: Google DeepMind releases PARDIG and SatWeave, the datasets behind WeatherNext 3
description:
Google DeepMind released the two foundational datasets behind its WeatherNext 3 forecasting model. PARDIG estimates global rainfall every 15 minutes and, per DeepMind, improves precipitation detection skill by more than 30%; SatWeave combines several geostationary satellites into one live view of Earth's clouds and storms every 60 minutes. The data is on Google Cloud Storage and Earth Engine (about 300 likes).

Why it matters: Researchers and startups get the observation data needed to build flood, wildfire-smoke and solar forecasting tools.

Tristan Harris worked at Google before devoting his life to saving humanity from AI. If half of what he says is true, we need to drop everything and fix this.



(00:00) Is AI Doomerism a Psyop?

Tristan is Co-Founder of the Center for Humane Technology (CHT), a nonprofit organization whose mission is to align technology with humanity’s best interests. He regularly briefs heads of state, technology CEOs, and US Congress members, in addition to mobilizing millions of people around the world through mainstream media. Tristan has explored the influences that hijack human attitudes, behaviors, and beliefs, from his childhood as a magician to his coursework in Stanford’s Persuasive Technology Lab to his leadership as a Design Ethicist at Google. Today, he studies how major technology platforms wield dangerous power over our ability to make sense of the world and leads the call for systemic change. title: Sean Stone’s 10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul
description:
10 Things to Learn: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul explores what it means to remain fully human in an age increasingly defined by technology, optimization, and artificial intelligence. While modern civilization has expanded humanity’s power and capability, it has done little to eliminate suffering, grief, fear, or the search for meaning. This book argues that life’s deepest questions cannot be answered through efficiency or control. Instead, genuine growth emerges through a series of essential initiations—moments of collapse, surrender, loss, rest, and devotion that shape the soul. Blending mythology, philosophy, memoir, and poetic reflection, it offers a timeless framework for navigating the emotional and spiritual disorientation of modern life.

Structured around ten symbolic “gates,” the book reframes life as a cyclical journey of awakening rather than a linear pursuit of success. These gates—Falling, Surrendering, Crying, Caring, Hating, Creating, Sharing, Loving, Breathing, and Laughing—each represent a threshold of psychological and spiritual transformation. Drawing from Greek mythology, Biblical narratives, Eastern philosophy, and archetypal storytelling, the book presents a unified map of human development. Its voice combines lyrical prose with intellectual rigor, placing it at the intersection of Joseph Campbell’s mythological insight, Alan Watts’s spiritual inquiry, and the literary introspection of Hermann Hesse.

At a time of accelerating technological change, rising anxiety, and the erosion of traditional sources of meaning, 10 Things to Learn offers something increasingly rare: not just insight, but initiation. It speaks to readers seeking coherence in a fragmented world and restores a sense of purpose through the defining ordeals of the human experience.

title: Of Bee Brains, ChatGPT, and Fists of Ham
description:
A Friday article at Science Daily caught my eye: “Scientists are Seriously Asking if Bees and ChatGPT Are Conscious.” Either the writer has been fuddled by an unholy amalgam of Cartesianism and materialism, or the framing is a sneaky rhetorical move to get the reader to think, “Wait, scientists don’t think a bee is conscious, but they are now open to the possibility? And ditto future AI?
